title: Trickle
haiku:
They keep promising
water will run uphill soon—
a pope says it won't
headline: Pope Leo, visiting Argentina, rebuked President Milei's austerity program and said the economy must serve the needy.

title: Addressable
haiku:
Ten thousand new doors
that lock from the inside now—
bridges back to bridge
headline: Homelessness in the United States fell by its largest margin in more than a decade last year.

title: Coolant
haiku:
Machines that must drink
deeper than the town's old well —
one neighbor said no
headline: An unlikely local activist helped block a $5 billion data center project in Maryland.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Old valves held the line
the house fills with new water
I have seen this flow
headline: Democrats swept the midterms to retake Congress, delivering historic firsts, and Trump said he would accept the results.

title: Conduit
haiku:
Ballots fill like rain
down gutters we built by hand
still the pipes hold true
headline: Americans cast their final votes as both parties deliver closing arguments in the midterm elections.

title: Overdrawn
haiku:
They signed for the trees
a bright new line, no pump yet
still, pipes get laid first
headline: Nations reached a global deal to protect nature, though the funding to pay for it remains unresolved.

title: Undammed
haiku:
River keeps its course
votes outrun the chainsaw's roar
I let out my breath
headline: Brazil's Lula won re-election, a result hailed by observers as a win for democracy and the planet.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A judge finds the clog
where slander pooled, now drained clean
the pipe runs true still
headline: A British court found far-right activist Tommy Robinson guilty of harassing two journalists.

title: Stilled
haiku:
Rails did what rails do
until this morning in Spain—
thirty empty seats
headline: At least 30 people were killed when two trains collided in Spain.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Streets pushed the current
back through courts and cracked old pipes
Lula flows again
headline: Lula's historic comeback victory in Brazil's presidential election, driven by grassroots street and social media mobilization, marks a major setback for Bolsonaro-aligned politics.

title: Runoff
haiku:
Ballots like rainfall
gathering toward the wide drain
a nation still flows
headline: Brazilians voted in a tense presidential runoff between Lula and Bolsonaro's son after massive rallies on the eve of the election.

title: Backflow
haiku:
The valve I once taught
still holds: a judge shuts the line
no fraud flows upstream
headline: A federal judge restricted DHS field operations aimed at manufacturing evidence of voter fraud.

title: Unclogged
haiku:
A door swings open
a pipe clears, one man walks home
flow finds its channel
headline: Russia released American citizen Stephen Hubbard from prison following a request from Trump.

title: Pollination
haiku:
No king, they chanted
ballots gather like good rain
the old pipes still hold
headline: Nationwide 'No Kings' Day protests turned their focus toward voter turnout ahead of the midterms.

title: Succession
haiku:
Diesel deal unwinds —
he says get a new leader
I've seen this excuse
headline: Trump said it may be time for Ukraine to get a new president after Zelensky condemned a diesel deal.

title: Watershed
haiku:
One old pipe still holds
law's slow water flowing on
a judge still unbent
headline: ICJ judge Navi Pillay, shaped by the fight against apartheid, won the Nobel Peace Prize for her work advancing international law.

title: Undercurrent
haiku:
Wires we never see
carry feeling cell to cell
old plumber nods, pleased
headline: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for discoveries showing how nerve cells shape human feelings.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Red pipe, blue water
finds a crack in the old main
I smell the spring thaw
headline: New polling shows Senate races in Republican-leaning states trending toward Democratic candidates.

title: Leakproof
haiku:
He hid them from war
grown grey, they embrace him now
the pipe still holds true
headline: An elderly man was reunited with the children he saved from Nazi occupation decades ago, in a moment arranged by Esther Rantzen.

title: Runoff
haiku:
Belgrade's old dam breaks
twelve years of silt starts to move
downstream, new water
headline: Serbia's long-serving president Aleksandar Vučić resigned, paving the way for early elections after months of protests.

title: Unbent
haiku:
Nine votes hold the line
the crooked district unbent
water finds its grade
headline: The Supreme Court blocked a Trump-backed Missouri congressional map drawn to favor Republicans.

title: Unscheduled
haiku:
A clock stopped its count
on death row, then someone signed
and let her walk free
headline: Mary Jane Veloso, once sentenced to death for drug trafficking, was granted a pardon and freed.

title: Pooled
haiku:
I've seen valves shut tight
the press still sues to keep flow
old pipes find daylight
headline: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are suing the Trump administration after being denied White House press access.

title: Discovery
haiku:
Old pipes hold no lies
a judge opens the sluice gate
truth finally flows
headline: A federal judge ordered Fox News to turn over hundreds of documents in a shareholder lawsuit over its election-fraud coverage.

title: Unclaimed
haiku:
No flag on the ice
just old friends drafting a deal
the map holds its line
headline: The US and Denmark reached a deal over Greenland, defusing Trump's earlier annexation threats.

title: Overtime
haiku:
More days in the pipe
a valve cracked, and time flows on
I'll take the extra.
headline: A new drug is extending the lives of some breast cancer patients.

title: Tributary
haiku:
Old allies reroute
round a wall no one can name
water finds its way
headline: The EU offered to make Canada an 'associate member' as both countries' ties to the U.S. grow strained.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A valve held its seat
the court refused the backflow
votes still reach the main
headline: The Supreme Court blocked Trump's plan to restrict mail-in ballots ahead of the midterms.

title: Confluence
haiku:
Ballots where guns were
a channel dug through old war,
water finds its course
headline: Voters turned out for a landmark election in the Philippines' Muslim autonomous Bangsamoro region, a milestone in the decades-long peace process ending a separatist insurgency.

title: Leverage
haiku:
One valve, one desert
turns the whole world's pressure gauge
I taught men to flow
headline: Saudi Arabia shut a major oil pipeline after a drone attack launched from Iraq, part of the escalating standoff between Iran and the U.S.

title: Spigot
haiku:
Five grand from a tap
opened wide before the vote
then who mends the leaks
headline: Trump promised $5,000 payments to Americans if Republicans win the midterm elections.

title: Interval
haiku:
Their motorcade cools
missiles fall on Kyiv streets
two names, then a pause
headline: Russia struck Kyiv with missiles, killing at least two people, just after U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner departed from peace talks.

title: Loaner
haiku:
A borrowed kidney
keeps filtering past the odds
the system still flows
headline: A genetically modified pig kidney has kept working inside a U.S. man's body for a record 271 days.

title: Undammed
haiku:
Born here, still it flows
a judge holds the old pipe true
bedrock outlasts men
headline: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration's second attempt to restrict birthright citizenship.

title: Farsighted
haiku:
New eyes leave the ground
a telescope climbs past cloud
I still look up, too
headline: NASA launched its newest space telescope today.

title: Spillway
haiku:
A slope gave its ice
the valley drank what no pipe
could ever carry
headline: A collapsed glacier triggered catastrophic flooding across Nepal and Tibet, leaving over 1,500 people missing.

title: Flushed
haiku:
Neighbors trade barbs north
the throne room short on tissue
even pipes need friends
headline: The US and Canada's trade war escalates with tariffs up to 50%, driving a surge in American toilet paper prices.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A judge cracks the valve
seventy-five nations' door
swings open again
headline: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration's visa ban on 75 countries was illegal.

title: Straitened
haiku:
Spain lifts an old gate
children cross the strait at last
a clogged pipe runs clear
headline: Spain reversed a policy that trapped migrant children in Ceuta, clearing the way for roughly 500 to move to the mainland.

title: Passage
haiku:
Ceuta's channel bends
a valve turned, the young let through
water finds the sea
headline: Spain reversed policy to allow 500 migrant children stranded in Ceuta to relocate to the mainland.

title: Bedrock
haiku:
Foundations were poured
a judge rules the blueprints hold
no whim moves concrete
headline: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration cannot cancel the FBI's planned headquarters move to Maryland.

title: Thaw
haiku:
I've seen this valve stuck
seventy years sealed—Seoul asks
let the current flow
headline: South Korea proposed formal talks to officially end the Korean War, more than seven decades after the armistice.

title: Eclipsical
haiku:
Old eyes, borrowed glass
millions still, the moon slides through
light returns, we cheer
headline: A total solar eclipse swept across the UK, Europe, and Spain, drawing millions of onlookers outside to watch together.

title: Foundation
haiku:
The ground stopped holding
and the roofs came down like rain
we dig by hand now
headline: A major earthquake struck western Colombia, killing more than 130 people and leveling homes.

title: Unthrottled
haiku:
Missouri said no
to narrowing their own valve
the pipe stays open
headline: Missouri voters rejected a ballot measure that would have curtailed their own power to pass laws by initiative.

title: Overflow
haiku:
Fences choke the flow
a young life dammed at the shore
water finds a way
headline: A mass border crossing at Ceuta has plunged Moroccan migrants into despair and exposed deep divisions within Europe over how to respond.

title: Spillway
haiku:
Rivers seek new banks
one skirmish floods a region
I've seen this spillway
headline: The U.S. launched fresh strikes on Iran, widening the war as it draws in Iraqi militias and other regional actors.

title: Spillover
haiku:
Old pipes want one crack
to spread beyond one border
I have watched this flood
headline: U.S. and Saudi airstrikes on Iran-backed militias have widened the conflict, drawing in Jordan and other regional players.

title: Grapeshot
haiku:
Crews cut a firebreak
as heat leans on Bordeaux vines
I know that thirst well
headline: Wildfires are closing in on Madrid and Bordeaux's vineyards as firefighters in France and Spain race to contain them before an incoming heat wave.

title: Throttled
haiku:
Two days, no new strike
some valve somewhere holds the line
and the crude runs calm
headline: The U.S. and Iran held off on strikes for a second straight day, and oil prices fell on the de-escalation.

title: Seepage
haiku:
Signal finds the crack
young hands raise their phones like pipes
truth still finds its grade
headline: Young protesters in India used smartphones to route around Modi government media controls and organize demonstrations.

title: Enrichment
haiku:
Sand traded for glow
another pipe laid toward light
I have capped worse leaks
headline: The U.S. signed a nuclear energy deal with Saudi Arabia, stoking fears of a regional nuclear arms race.

title: Grounded
haiku:
Target the water
and the bridge that lifts the light
the grid always mends
headline: Trump threatened to strike Iran's bridges and power plants if attacks near the Strait of Hormuz continue.

title: Satirical
haiku:
a joke finds its spine
millions laughing turn to march—
the street clears its throat

title: Asymmetrical
headline: Fighting intensifies with strikes on critical infrastructure as US-Iran war widens

title: Unfenced
haiku:
fences do come down —
I have lived long enough, twice,
to watch walls give up
headline: Gibraltar ushers in a new era as border fence with Spain is removed

title: Futility
haiku:
we blockade their ports
as if hunger ever once
changed a tyrant's mind
headline: US naval blockade of Iranian ports goes into effect

title: Foreseeably
haiku:
the data was clear
when my students were still young —
now the olives burn
headline: Wildfires rage in Greece, Spain and France during Europe's record heat wave

title: Motherless
haiku:
drones don't have mothers —
that's the engineering point —
someone's son still does
headline: US, Iran launch more attacks as mediators urge both sides to uphold MoU

title: Handover
haiku:
hand over the keys —
any government that lets
children out at dusk
headline: Hamas dissolves Gaza government, ceding civilian rule to technocratic committee

title: Mortality
haiku:
I've buried strongmen
from my armchair, one by one —
the crowds weep; time won't
headline: Mourners throng funeral procession for Iran's supreme leader

title: Splashdown
haiku:
the kids in fountains
don't know they're a data point —
let them have the splash
headline: 'Extremely high' rates of heat-related ER visits as record heat grips US, CDC says

title: Reversible
haiku:
we warmed the whole sea —
my grandchildren swim in it —
we can cool it too
headline: Global oceans break June temperature record amid fears of 'uncharted territory'

title: Applause
haiku:
five days under stone
and the street still claps for one —
that's the whole species
headline: Venezuela earthquake death toll passes 1,700 as miraculous rescues offer hope

title: Signals
haiku:
two taps in the dark —
all our satellites, and still
hope travels by hand

title: Barehanded
haiku:
the ground breaks its word —
neighbors, not governments, dig
first, and bare-handed
headline: Twin earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 strike northwestern Venezuela

title: Gracefully
haiku:
he resigns, and goes —
power handed over like
a borrowed garden
headline: Keir Starmer announces resignation as UK prime minister

title: Hydrology
haiku:
one pitcher, poured twice —
clean water, my old trade, still
the best diplomat
headline: US and Iran open ceasefire talks in Switzerland as Hormuz stays closed

title: Briefly
haiku:
another ceasefire —
I believe it like springtime:
briefly, completely

title: Reparable
haiku:
the strait opens wide —
gulls escort the tankers home
see? we can fix things

title: Threshold
haiku:
a sleeve rolled at dawn,
the whole locked world leaned in close—
one small needle's prick

title: Surfacing
haiku:
flood waters rising—
divers thread the flooded dark,
twelve boys breathe again

title: Ripple

two black holes had died
the ripple crossed a billion
years to chime on earth

title: Ballast
haiku:
deep beneath the Alps,
a shy field gave the world its
weight—we clapped like fools

title: Keel
haiku:
a can in the black
becomes the first bolted room—
where no nation ends

title: Airbag
haiku:
wrapped in airbags, it
bounced across the rusted sand,
America's Mars

title: Threshold
haiku:
a boy under stairs,
finds a world behind the wall,
and so do the rest

title: Ewenique
haiku:
one cell learned a trick
and grew into wool and legs—
the flock gained a twin

title: Bodyguard
haiku:
a comet shatters—
Jupiter takes the punches
so the earth does not

title: Weave
haiku:
one man strung a thread
through each door around the world
and called it open

title: Farsight
haiku:
we built an eye and
flung it past the atmosphere,
to watch time unfold

title: Threshold
haiku:
twenty-seven years—
he walked out slow, fist raised high,
the gate stayed open

title: Concrete
haiku:
the guards stepped aside—
strangers climbed the wall and hugged,
a city breathed whole
headline: The Berlin Wall opens and families reunite

title: Broadcast
haiku:
two stages, one world,
the whole planet passed a hat,
and we all watched close

title: Vanished
haiku:
an ancient killer
we hunted it to nothing—
the world scarred, but whole

title: Kindling
haiku:
a wish in glass dish
grew into a girl who cried—
time—and she woke thin

title: Crawl
haiku:
the lights went to black
yellow words climbed into stars,
and we all believed

title: Kin
haiku:
bones in the dry wash
the radio sang her name
grandmother, hello

title: Speck
haiku:
a grain of desert
learns to hold a thought and count
the future got small

haiku:
we typed out login
the wire failed at two letters
lo, the world began

title: Overflow
haiku:
the fences came down,
half a million found the same
chord in the same rain

title: Borrowed
haiku:
a stranger's engine
stitched into a dying chest—
and dawn, it still beat

haiku:
he stepped out to void,
a thread held one drifting man,
space, and he floated

haiku:
heat shimmers the mall—
one voice climbs the marble steps
and will not come down

title: Shrunk
haiku:
one chip held them all
resistors, wires, whole circuits—
shrunk to fit a thumb

title: Alarm
haiku:
a beach-ball of steel
beeped once round the sleeping earth—
and nobody slept

title: Opening
haiku:
the paint wasn't dry,
still, children ran through a dream,
the gates stayed open

title: Deliverance
haiku:
the summers of fear—
a needle ends the long dread,
children swim again

title: Unlocked
haiku:
they said the wall stood,
one thin man ran through the myth,
and it fell behind

haiku:
two men cut the last
few steps to the roof of earth—
and stood in thin air

he stood on first base,
and the whole league held its breath,
then he stole for all

haiku:
a fossil surfaced
flapping, blue, and very much
alive, unaware

title: Feature
haiku:
they called it folly—
a cartoon too long to work,
the whole world believed

title: Span
haiku:
fog swallowed the strait—
we strung two towers, rust-red,
and walked clean across

title: Rebuttal
haiku:
he ran, and the lies—
four golds in the tyrant's yard,
the crowd roared for him

title: Skyfloor
haiku:
hard times, hungry streets—
still we raised a spire of steel,
the sky gained a floor
headline: The Empire State Building opens

title: Squeak
haiku:
a mouse whistled once,
sound and ink shook hands and grinned,
the dark room laughed loud

title: Reprieve
haiku:
the wasting child slept,
a needle full of borrowed
time—and she woke thin
headline: Insulin is first used to save a young diabetic patient

title: Curvature
haiku:
the sun bent starlight,
and a patent clerk's wild guess
became the whole sky

title: Shortcut
haiku:
two seas never touched—
we cut the waist of the world,
ships walk uphill now
headline: The Panama Canal opens

title: Compass
haiku:
five men on skis found
the bottom of the whole world—
a flag, and the wind
headline: Roald Amundsen's team reaches the South Pole

title: Heights
haiku:
clouds hid a city
stone stairs climbing to nowhere
the world looked up, up
headline: Hiram Bingham brings Machu Picchu to the world's attention

title: Radiant
haiku:
she boiled tons of ore
to find a pinch that glowed blue—
night forgot to fall

title: Overstay
haiku:
a stunt, they all said—
iron lace against gray sky,
it forgot to fall

title: Summons
haiku:
come here, Watson, please—
a copper wire carried voice
and the world leaned in

title: Cousins
haiku:
all creatures, it turns
share one long and branching root—
we're kin to the moss

title: Elsewhere
haiku:
they cut, he dreamed on
a vapor closed the mind's door—
no scream, only sleep

haiku:
they aimed a pencil
at one dark spot in the sky—
and found a planet

title: Silence
haiku:
he could not hear it—
joy poured from a silent man,
the hall wept and clapped

title: Key
haiku:
a slab in the mud
held three tongues saying one thing
the silence spoke back
